Glottolog's URL for it (ic.payap.ac.th/.) now returns 404; the PDF was recovered from the the Internet Archive (2019 snapshot of inter.payap.ac.th) and is also listed at archive.org/details/245-jejara (same 4,531,599-byte file).

sources.citation: Barkman, Tiffany. 2014. A descriptive grammar of Jejara (Para Naga). MA thesis, Payap University, Chiang Mai. xxi+222 pp. (245-page PDF)
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Silent on stress. Ch. 2 'Phonology and morphology' (thesis pp. 19-28 = pp. 41-50) is a self-described 'cursory overview' whose consonant, vowel and tone charts are copied from Lubbe (2007, unpublished orthography statement). 2.2.3 Tone (p. 21): three tones (mid/high/low) with minimal pairs; 'Tone is, however, not as robust as in some languages, and there are not a great number of minimal pairs showing contrast only by tone.' 2.4 Syllable and word structure (p. 22): C1(C2)V, no codas, words 1-3 syllables, prenasalization and 'minor syllable' noted as needing further study.
